segments: Fifth Jubilee.
The Kings of the Medes and Persians.
[After] Belshazzar, Darius the Mede, who is Nabonidus, [ruled] one year after he killed Belshazzar;
for he was sixty-six years old then, as king.
And in that year he set Daniel above all the magnates.
And on this account Daniel was envied and cast into the lions' den the first time.
And when he was delivered,
they perished.
After Darius the Mede {OCR?}, Cyrus the Persian [ruled] thirty-one years;
and in other copies, nine;
and in other copies, three.
When this man killed Darius the Mede,
he brought an end to the kingdom of the Chaldeans, Assyrians, and Medes,
and established the kingdom of the Persians,
and made his dwelling in Babylon.
He also appointed the faithful Daniel over the affairs of the kingdom.
And Daniel was zealous and smashed the idol of Bel, the god of the Babylonians—
he was the first king of the Chaldeans, the father of Ninus who built Nineveh.
And furthermore, that Daniel killed the dragon.
And he was hated by the Babylonians,
and cast into the den in which there were seven lions.
This was the second time,
when the prophet Habakkuk was sent from Judea
and brought him food.
And he was delivered again from the lions,
and his enemies perished.
Now Daniel, when he counted the years of captivity and thought that the seventy years decreed upon the people by the word of the Lord through Jeremiah were already fulfilled,
fasted and prayed for twenty-one days, asking for the return of the people.
Then he saw a fearful vision by the river Tigris:
a man clothed in fine linen, and he said to him:
"Behold, it has been twenty-one days that I have been contending against the ruler of the Persians;"
